# Lunacy in the Cloud with Diamonds

*Entering the age of the White Album*

**Author:** Claus Aasholm  
**Published:** May 05, 2026  
**Source:** [https://clausaasholm.substack.com/p/lunacy-in-the-cloud-with-diamonds](https://clausaasholm.substack.com/p/lunacy-in-the-cloud-with-diamonds)

---

While I am old, it is not so bad that I grew up in the glory days of the Fab Four from Liverpool. While my father was listening to Dixie Jazz, he picked up the habit while serving as a soldier stationed in the US (our countries were closer then, and we provided our allies with the needed protection), my mother wore out the cheap record player we had with Beatles songs. It was in the days with matching suits, hairdo, and “She Loves You, yeah, yeah”. Very unlikely to scare your grandmother. I was never a Beatles fan, but it was part of the musical soup I grew up in. The lyrics were really the only exposure I had to English in my early years, a language that today is so deep in me that I begin to dream in English after spending a couple of days in England. While my English is good, I am still far from being bilingual. That is in a class of its own, as those of my readers with parents who speak different native tongues will know.

I began formal English education at 12, but then it was too late. My English language and my writing would forever be slightly unhinged from reality. The Beatles’ story also resonates with me as I have learned to accept that everything goes from orderly to complex over time. When you have learned to manage the new complexity and begin to view it as orderly, it descends into new complexity. The only option for me was to make complexity my friend and welcome the new disorder. From the cellars of Hamburg, the Beatles became idols and then a global phenomenon that both imprisoned and liberated them, personally and artistically. The rest of their career together would be an attempt to escape that prison, and maybe why Paul and Wings made “Band on the Run”. While I was still a kid when the White Album was made, it was a piece of plastic that had a profound impact on me over the years, and it kept revealing deeper layers of meaning, something John mocked in “Glass Onion” while pretending there was no meaning. The Beatles had begun their moustachioed, spiritually curious journey into a passive-aggressive, brilliant studio-wizard band, but the White Album exposed the insanity. It is a marvellous product of deep disagreement and mutual dislike. Every song is a battle between John and Paul, while George is desperately trying to become one of

them or Eric Clapton, while Ringo is trying to ignore them all, eating a biscuit. The album is messy and chaotic, and it sounds like it was made by 30 different bands. It did not come as a complete surprise, Sgt. Pepper and the Lonely Hearts Band was a warning about what was about to come. While John denied that Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds was a reference to a psychedelic drug, the writers certainly had more than a bad piece of chicken when writing it. I don’t know what Rocking Horse People are, but I know they eat Marshmallow Pie while The Girl with Kaleidoscope eyes is watching the Marmalade Skies and Plasticine Porters with Looking Glass Ties. Right now, it looks like the AI revolution that has made the semiconductor market far more complex is about to enter its next, more chaotic phase, two and a half years after it began. Leaving Sgt. Pepper to enter the White insanity era. While the cloud market has always been intricately connected to the semiconductor market, they can be viewed and analysed individually; that is about to end as the two markets merge into a higher level of complexity, but it might not be as insane as I thought when I first saw it.

Apart from the groundbreaking decision by Google and Amazon to enter the Semiconductor Device market by making their own AI Chips generally available, there were several other key developments. The Agentic revolution is now visible, and the added inference workload will benefit Intel and AMD, as well as hyperscaler AI architectures purposely designed for this. All of the hyperscalers promoted that their customers have seen increased performance gains through agents. This drives a new business model from “Seat” to “Seat plus Consumption”, which sounds like selling rubber bands by the yard. A new level of trust is needed for that one. While the agentic workflow will impact the semiconductor industry, there is still limited tangible evidence to work with, so I will address that later. There were also significant developments in physical AI, with more than 500K Google Waymo rides a week and 2M miles driven by Amazon Zoox. There were also the first signs of robotics activity. Amazon pledged 20 more launches in 26 and 30 in 27, adding to the first 10 launches that have brought 250 Project Leo satellites into orbit. A major strategic development in this space is Amazon’s planned acquisition of Globalstar. This acquisition provides Amazon with the scarce global spectrum and satellite expertise required to offer direct-to-device capabilities.

Amazon is leveraging this acquisition to establish a deep relationship with Apple. Amazon Leo will now natively power direct-to-device satellite services for Apple iPhones and Apple Watches. Open space is now open for business. The 4 major AI companies all decided to coordinate their earnings releases into a few hours. While this is a coincidence, it gave the markets a chance to respond rather than the normal flip-flopping between the calls.

In what is seasonally a down quarter, the 4 main hyperscalers grew revenue by over 20%, while profits increased compared to Q4.

Google's cloud revenue growth has been astonishing and demonstrates the benefits of having a full tech stack, from chips to native models. While Microsoft could claim the same, I have not heard of anyone using Co-Pilot unless they are forced by a corporate purchasing decision. While I have not tried it, I imagine an LLM with a lot of buttons and menus that ignores the user experience. I apologise for letting my bias briefly peek through. The CapEx increased again, but was weaker than last quarters 21% growth. Quite astonishing to hear myself say that 9% QoQ is weak, but we have been spoiled over the last few years. As most of the memory contracts are long-term agreements, it is probably still too early to see the effect on CapEx.

The CapEx guidance was strong across all major hyperscalers and was immediately reflected in the consensus of financial analysts. While the future CapEx growth shows that the financial analysts know as much as my hairdresser about the 2027 forecast, they still have to run the numbers. They do, however, have a firm grip on the near-term forecast for 2026, which rose from 66% to 79% growth in just one quarter. That is another $50B on top of the $250B forecasted last quarter. Soon, we'll be talking real money, as Warren Buffett would say.

Undoubtedly, we are seeing the impact of memory pricing on the CapEx forecast, and as memory contracts evolve from one- to multiyear agreements, the hyperscalers all have a pretty good idea of the near-term impact. This is a problem emerging for the hyperscalers. One thing is that memory pricing is increasing dramatically, another is that it is rising due to high demand and low capacity. It is impossible to expand a data centre without allocating memory, and that should have been sorted out yesterday or the year before. Up until now, the bottleneck has been GPUs, but rumours have it that they are not yet fully utilised, the power scarcity set in, and now it's memory. As I have said before, there are alternatives in power but not in memory. That the hyperscalers have been working on securing memory is obvious when plotting their purchasing commitments:

The overall backlog for the hyperscalers increased by $444B, a whopping 40% in just one quarter. This is what hyperscalers are trying to intercept, and why CapEx is exploding. While the backlog is not guaranteed to add to existing revenue, this is the normal procedure. Microsoft states that the duration of the backlog deals is typically 2.5 years, and if this is expanded across the board, this is the revenue impact the current backlog will have on the cloud revenue.

It is pretty astonishing given that the revenue could all be additive to the current revenue. Microsoft believes it can convert 25% of its backlog to revenue within a year, while Google expect to convert 50% within two years, which seems to align with each other. While the numbers are as insane as the white album, the actions of the cloud companies are quite rational. They are trying to intercept a massive order opportunity through investments. Anthropic and OpenAI are significant contributors to the backlog, but it is extending beyond the Natives as the workload moves towards inference.

## Cloud Full Hardware Stack

One of the most intersting developments of this cloud earnings round was that the home-bred compute chips of the Hyperscalers are ready to leave home. While this has been underway, it has become very visible this time around. It is no secret that Cloud Compute Chips already run a significant proportion of inference workloads, and at Google, they also run the internal training workloads for Gemini. While Google has the least dependence on Nvidia, the full-stack AI company is delivering Nvidia instances via Google Cloud and supporting workloads that need CUDA.

Amazon landed over 2.1 million AI Chips over the last 12 months, of which half were Trainium chips. The custom chip business has surpassed a $20B annual revenue run rate. Amazon's CEO noted that if this were a stand-alone operation selling chips to both AWS and third parties, it would have an annual run rate of $50 billion, making it one of the top three data centre chip businesses in the world. Google is not yet recognising any revenue from external chip sales and does not expect to do so before the end of 2026, with real volumes being shipped in 2027. The scales of the Cloud Compute Chips can be seen compared to tier two suppliers below:

![Figure from page 25](https://private-us-east-1.manuscdn.com/sessionFile/CP7bzSa4UNzdm23jbPqGGm/sandbox/nwPet4QPfRYFFG0HTToRnb-images_1778933107729_na1fn_L2hvbWUvdWJ1bnR1L3BkZl9tYXJrZG93bl9jb252ZXJzaW9uL2Fzc2V0cy9maWd1cmVfMTJfcGFnZV8yNQ.png?__&Key-Pair-Id=K2HSFNDJXOU9YS&Signature=lKIQrPFXZlnu7~2U9oVLMsF5QLJBbG2czz8n6Awyk~NBA3hfcxViigizcie8W7Tq-AkC-6-R3jPvErydRvgYJ6CAonaptnrmNpOzR87b4B5-B-xu3I-Q~2ZKjL1ETMSDa2qo2-ccxjwNLWMJ94KMun0-yjpW9NM9SchjYcHv6aMu1Hg8okAHDkX7YETVzYMjITLhanMzXx~SpfpTz~cshS3aYQJjZ~tsE2bQL7BSdIuFkR-sSdRErN-4PGYZPiSxptIHSrd2XIDrjVXYrsyU~jldZEVbZe1D36vVbYjlLA1nWF9IkqDmMcUg3xPwahgiWj4-DhloIx1vkIw9leH-jg__)

While Nvidia is still way ahead with 50B$ in Datacenter compute in Q1 of 2026, the hyperscalers’ entry into the semiconductor industry is significant and will once again render the feeble attempts to forecast overall semiconductor industry revenue useless. The graphs are not an apples-to-apples comparison, as Marvel and Broadcom supply some chips to hyperscalers. While they make an effort to sound like the main supplier of computers, this quarter's information makes that very unlikely. The compute revenue numbers are too small to account for the main compute components, while the story is more true for the other parts of the server chipset. The next natural question that arises is who is going to buy Google's and Amazon's chips. Amazon could reveal deals with Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and Uber, while Google is limited to Anthropic at the moment. Long-term, this will be expanded broadly to enterprise customers, with Apple as an obvious candidate. Amazon already has a 225B$ commitment towards its chips, which is significant.

![Figure from page 27](https://private-us-east-1.manuscdn.com/sessionFile/CP7bzSa4UNzdm23jbPqGGm/sandbox/nwPet4QPfRYFFG0HTToRnb-images_1778933107729_na1fn_L2hvbWUvdWJ1bnR1L3BkZl9tYXJrZG93bl9jb252ZXJzaW9uL2Fzc2V0cy9maWd1cmVfMTNfcGFnZV8yNw.png?__&Key-Pair-Id=K2HSFNDJXOU9YS&Signature=raqYBEY-8YSqug5GnnmV2Ym6fDugv5t5ZkNNSLTq7lZ3n3m6zMyBo0P5DgwJL35RVNcHDsjWgayK56Yx~L7YI1f~cJfqy75ovKojbPxO9WWkgKLeUo9YGtJ7d12xhkII6S8rXnab5RpGwThZIQlYOYq8Eyav68DTb2J2OHTcA8ErPcF6eBgUjA8nsuigs7QcWPFPTplIp4yrh0FBGRhpyhvE9MqZxYOqpsoFKydfn-TOtc2wNu-HOLnb3q7kI2uNQ7f8MeGqYwy-w~CbrO02oRzxrFmmr8-GWRR0RidWbmYeeoba51KuMsM7S5wih-M008ic29mZbi8Mz9g5Is644Q__)

It is intersting that Meta is also a customer despite having its own architectures, but this is pretty much in line with the emerging strategies of betting on all horses. Not only is Meta building its own capacity, but it is also booking capacity elsewhere. It is also flip-flopping on employees, from billion-dollar paychecks to having multiple thousands of firing slips in the mail at the same time. It seems like Meta is still moving fast and breaking things before they have even been tested. Fortunately for Meta, the business is healthy and can handle some strategic detours. One of the most consequential developments this quarter is that Meta is rolling out its AI products to its user base, which is significantly larger than OpenAI’s. ChatGPT claims 900m users while Meta has close to 4B users a day. As I have said, “Half of the cloud companies have decided to market their internally used AI Semiconductor devices and become semiconductor companies”, some of my readers will say, “Yeah, we know!” If I were running a newsletter, we could stop here and get a cup of tea and a biscuit. But since I am pushing analysis rather than news, we will have to continue to the next natural strategic question: “Why?”

![Figure from page 28](https://private-us-east-1.manuscdn.com/sessionFile/CP7bzSa4UNzdm23jbPqGGm/sandbox/nwPet4QPfRYFFG0HTToRnb-images_1778933107729_na1fn_L2hvbWUvdWJ1bnR1L3BkZl9tYXJrZG93bl9jb252ZXJzaW9uL2Fzc2V0cy9maWd1cmVfMTRfcGFnZV8yOA.png?__&Key-Pair-Id=K2HSFNDJXOU9YS&Signature=m4IHCGba8Kya7ikZDQzN-MksBhm7Zpm6g4XPI7pxgA2e6QPNWNzeqpkWljLWBmOjERHywonfG4kzOx6nGfVo3c6yxAgS72lFmD5y2Ybtc6mSYB1nT0NArauB7z8P8-zBemTDY92mxe8Bdyz2UsDd9uVRSp-TRBGbr50ohD3PYArAa98r1NPydNa-yMGDt2vErC669xnr4zEm~QGkX4Xb0i8paschSpPMb-VQBMrYWnSUHjBVepOTZe8PfG2Ajo4Ac~5Ee6DQQAo3yb373iBFCSG~vQWNYvT44wFxZpiGiC-~MbcwLSFXu8TP447-8a~Wkf4E9KvkYrwHc46-21fFCw__)

To answer this question, we need to move from revenue and profits to cash flow and free cash flow. Before you start yawning and thinking, "My accountant needs to deal with this!", cash flow analysis is one of the most lethal weapons in finance. My personal corporate experience is that I pitched an expansion of sales territory with new sales offices and failed a couple of times until I received formal finance training and was able to present the project's cash flows alongside revenue and profitability. Companies don’t fold as a result of negative profits; they fold as they run out of cash, and the most enjoyable teacher is a young, geeky Jeff Bezos trying to explain to the world that Amazon is a great company despite never making a profit. To this day, Amazon still reports Cash Flow first as the only company I follow. While the profit and loss ledger provides a good view of profitability over a given period, it is not a great way to understand a long-term project like the construction of a data centre. A rough model of the construction of a 1 GW data centre is shown below

As shown, the project begins with a significant CapEx investment. Here, I have used a 35B investment over two years. These are followed by a couple of upgrade cycles as the servers degrade compared to the newest available kit. Revenue climbs with utilisation rate and declines as overall computing costs fall over time, while operational costs remain relatively flat.

![Figure from page 30](https://private-us-east-1.manuscdn.com/sessionFile/CP7bzSa4UNzdm23jbPqGGm/sandbox/nwPet4QPfRYFFG0HTToRnb-images_1778933107729_na1fn_L2hvbWUvdWJ1bnR1L3BkZl9tYXJrZG93bl9jb252ZXJzaW9uL2Fzc2V0cy9maWd1cmVfMTVfcGFnZV8zMA.png?__&Key-Pair-Id=K2HSFNDJXOU9YS&Signature=WHpj7n6Bb7mZFrq0lNyYMFt0R-zgRqZg9o-DqiSeWL~1iQGkymLDkmFabkANkQbbblYxiGjOJzZMBG-GenYhtPGgWlLvE6YZb7715FJkEgIlodXOuxNFEdSGzZ-hmc1OuLh-MsytRmRpTuMNbgLdZitAUMebSniiCmcjuNlV9R~IFH86ZrJ9y3~4PVcpK3xK13N~fzDNDYGfd5bgTRxuIfIvpwTZ6bPTtY13QEJ78smedAVkxmXv1GGaUESHcgGHzlhvZn6NgbWAIvFDbnUZtIhj3S90RrlZ5j3kAwa44BD0Sea3I7WId9TtLgpL8fJp6qjls14Zff-M6xa4i~arWA__)

Three years after inception, the Cloud data centre is very profitable, and all is good. Before getting slapped by my finance friends, I have to state that I have not included the cost of capital, and I do understand WACC and discounting. This is for illustration purposes only. The resulting free cash flow and cumulative free cash flow can be seen below:

![Figure from page 32](https://private-us-east-1.manuscdn.com/sessionFile/CP7bzSa4UNzdm23jbPqGGm/sandbox/nwPet4QPfRYFFG0HTToRnb-images_1778933107729_na1fn_L2hvbWUvdWJ1bnR1L3BkZl9tYXJrZG93bl9jb252ZXJzaW9uL2Fzc2V0cy9maWd1cmVfMTZfcGFnZV8zMg.png?__&Key-Pair-Id=K2HSFNDJXOU9YS&Signature=OyhNG30UOpxf8v~EMlm2aL7fEhBPP3nrephk2KnCi0ikZK7C-PICgcH8T5Hm317bEooPmPan~R0bDjToqua8oEyNR5s21HriDTYfA4370DfazaD4F7-A6eVRAxRUYa0i7TmqL0bGj9JR5RaReLSbvQG0GF8LApNP2kXoIA3m-caoXBBQbcDwILdDFK2LscUKBlaF05UoL-7DW1WuZwMm6pXjUPKO80bMk0J3e3j~jWvY6TG2XKiWK0cmY~41mg2-bImhS0GCh~9A5wgqC9C-KYkJYjxXGy-rXY4EHzWyF5FueKwJWxv2E4hzLDiwklMBnfG1y5FSRqSYm~puDYh0fw__)

While the 1 GW data centre is in positive cash flow after 2 years, the cumulative cash flow remains negative for almost 6 years. If you are in the data centre building business, you need solid operating cash flow to fund it, or you will have to find alternative sources of financing. In an earlier post, I highlighted this issue for the large cloud companies. The Cloudy Semiconductor Market Driver CLAUS AASHOLM · 2月24日 Read full story Using Consensus revenue and CapEx to calculate free cash flow, it is clear that in this year, Amazon and Meta will no longer be able to pay the bills, and Google's free cash flow will follow suit; only Microsoft can carry the investment for now.

The massive investments in 2024 and 2025 have been funded by retained earnings, and as a result, debt has remained flat.

![Figure from page 34](https://private-us-east-1.manuscdn.com/sessionFile/CP7bzSa4UNzdm23jbPqGGm/sandbox/nwPet4QPfRYFFG0HTToRnb-images_1778933107729_na1fn_L2hvbWUvdWJ1bnR1L3BkZl9tYXJrZG93bl9jb252ZXJzaW9uL2Fzc2V0cy9maWd1cmVfMTdfcGFnZV8zNA.png?__&Key-Pair-Id=K2HSFNDJXOU9YS&Signature=fRSUrQ7UrtUrICh2ovCZsNPkpQ~UD8~FhUUlf7ov~YtsfIuc1IdG6k7elpsJW~az-AZZJlmVYA75H5OjNF~t8fthdqXUrQ4TxPrq-8rtlPjQoaurghJ2QKYO1cmkcBwLzr~l4Xq7h-Gyaoary14SOerAosBAkxRldVIZfkbbLTKeyN~UJ2ywYhK041MJqmnCmpv8vq8AHN931KSnhjpmmXn3CS5IGMNqG6hHYcRb46HG5KvZw~QCCN3OrVFc5leU32Tdd8jcpJbvrwmV-3LKUXK~D3b1HtE7QKr1X429yVrrFwwqBdh3DlZw4ENCMvGzJejdMhoHNcwwAf3UBlAAJw__)

This is changing in Q1-2026. While Google, Microsoft and Meta were able to carry the load in the first quarter, Amazon experienced negative cash flow as predicted and decided to almost double its debt from 66B$ to 119B$. Google added $31B in debt, or roughly the CapEx of a 1 GW data centre.

![Figure from page 36](https://private-us-east-1.manuscdn.com/sessionFile/CP7bzSa4UNzdm23jbPqGGm/sandbox/nwPet4QPfRYFFG0HTToRnb-images_1778933107729_na1fn_L2hvbWUvdWJ1bnR1L3BkZl9tYXJrZG93bl9jb252ZXJzaW9uL2Fzc2V0cy9maWd1cmVfMThfcGFnZV8zNg.png?__&Key-Pair-Id=K2HSFNDJXOU9YS&Signature=avWGRBgun19h9jlydy4qGuCHJI2szetUHil5S7G4~PUPN7Yl1wWsvrH0ZYGtIMFlnoM~YytUeRpLZlswbW3KOYKEpQb61c3EBATQhvaGoWsrqj3k3TudRkQIVMGeAdos8W6I4sEJ0Zl~r7gSJd5dI-n4iwwUSSn6n~yhsaEwk2XxmhRNDPEHoHr0MdgnyOXP9Vyf0pmINslwVXldny05kRfZoDqBJyMvEmjlUJSZDL1-38LTpKBYzaPI-~FQliZ6M1Kd28-AHZHDdNr4lZz2CIRUBeB~vl8Y6XHDZgfGwoaM3xvQttIg1JtqMS4E9haEi7w3e1gUznFqKeJoTPlGgA__)

This is far from a signal that Amazon or any of the others are in trouble, but it does represent a strategic shift towards debt financing led by Amazon, with the rest expected to follow, except Microsoft for now.

![Figure from page 38](https://private-us-east-1.manuscdn.com/sessionFile/CP7bzSa4UNzdm23jbPqGGm/sandbox/nwPet4QPfRYFFG0HTToRnb-images_1778933107729_na1fn_L2hvbWUvdWJ1bnR1L3BkZl9tYXJrZG93bl9jb252ZXJzaW9uL2Fzc2V0cy9maWd1cmVfMTlfcGFnZV8zOA.png?__&Key-Pair-Id=K2HSFNDJXOU9YS&Signature=cdhRQB5DCBufhEQsc7t3iAoiQ20Uxeai4qUPGK95ACcGtKrl3SwuRb-0SgTMfcUhaK-VWf61c7GiaPaPkPwIOjcw0B~aogxJ9M35MT2idjj~BMJPDt5FCEPViT0Z823pI24SYzo2odM~u2DicT5idT~avBtIUqAPUg7uB0lyULZ3QElTU9uz89aCdsOvDk52U9GW6syoUsLWubH-ijMC-olxZHHe~11d1AC7Nntpd6jOPYhnwH6ANBnkYNO-5FiH1GR1yxNOyX-tUArZ3ll1rEQbnaBxCIDlsStvrEHxRYyqJZ4LbECgHdrmqD7NwnFjmp~sqCjgQ9~1nE97Zk7yfQ__)

One way to analyse companies' debt levels is to plot Net Debt against Operating profit. All hyperscalers are still below the Dow's non-financial normal level, but soon the investment decision will no longer be an exclusively internal one and will require external approval. The new operating strategy is a deliberate decision by Amazon, and it carries a number of implications. First of all, Amazon does not have to invest beyond its retained earnings, but has chosen to do so. The AI race is still very much on, and Amazon wants to put the pedal to the metal. In principle, the debt Amazon has raised is more than sufficient to carry the company through the next 7 quarters if the analyst consensus holds:

![Figure from page 40](https://private-us-east-1.manuscdn.com/sessionFile/CP7bzSa4UNzdm23jbPqGGm/sandbox/nwPet4QPfRYFFG0HTToRnb-images_1778933107729_na1fn_L2hvbWUvdWJ1bnR1L3BkZl9tYXJrZG93bl9jb252ZXJzaW9uL2Fzc2V0cy9maWd1cmVfMjBfcGFnZV80MA.png?__&Key-Pair-Id=K2HSFNDJXOU9YS&Signature=YVetAq6VMiSPer3ZnjgP6mgjAg~BavNDiLmiKNxF1YMHlfU9cjFN-a4VmXl723NrdZd6t6xVjcK8qsUchHbgtTJ9h8jq7VXXZ7dAuoB76-CP1b8TQY2-mmz8vZbzxTRX1Lwc-hX~h8JYtSUWvnGWiuzbln3DVsPWklCgDdyE8Ih5IcWg3ejvS62tybs9n99Jg5FsFE6zKcmSr-HdanyNRxhjdQu-uUjHUxfr9dHn9SbLHigK9yuNiaX9A9n0ZtB9ZP-fLlbLDZeQ57ERwb9UTSoPoNEXds8k0WZfv0~oFbbtBMhvRt7fqdR6uSK92kgQgCgOdKZZwvRNtxjphfAyyA__)

Amazon will need $34B to fuel the next 9 quarters before an anticipated cash flow boost from the current buildout. As the company just raised $53B and now has cash reserves of more than $100B, it is good to go. Still, the Orange Trinkets and Bit Barn have decided to sell the crown jewels, and Google has decided to follow. Internally designed and manufactured chips are always most profitably deployed by the hyperscaler owner. It costs money to sell and market them, and there has to be room for profit for the customer. If you conduct a profit-and-loss analysis, it is obvious that you should deploy the chips internally and reap the profits. The Cash Flow analysis highlights the “time to positive cash flow problem that needs to be dealt with. Selling Chips gives the two companies an additional revenue stream to build on, and the return comes much faster than building a data centre (which they will certainly continue to do). Chip revenue can also continue even if Amazon or Google has to delay datacenter buildouts due to a lack of memory or power. They can sell to the lucky ones who have planned their way out of these issues.

While it is certainly a move to curtail Nvidia's power, which extends far beyond GPUs, it is more plausible that this is an attempt to intercept the backlog that both Amazon and Google are building at a pace they cannot service with their current CapEx. We are most likely at the beginning of an even crazier investment phase than the one we are seeing right now. For Amazon specifically, it could be a problem that not enough memory has been ordered, which could limit internal growth. While the Graviton CPU can run on external DDR5, the trainiums and Interferentia’s needs HBMs onboard. The Graviton does not rely on Amazon for memory and could be sold to anyone who has secured a DDR5 supply. No matter what, the semiconductor market has once again undergone a rapid and significant increase in complexity, and top-line revenue numbers are becoming increasingly irrelevant as semiconductor companies sell to each other. Memory companies are selling HBMs to Compute companies, while Marvell and Broadcom are selling devices to hyperscalers, who both use and sell them to other cloud companies. All of the computing companies are evolving from devices to systems to full server systems, making device revenue somewhat irrelevant. The complexity is going towards lunacy. Towards white noise.

But who cares? Complexity is my friend, and I will be back, with a little help from my friends.
